note: Morton County Parks recreation area on Sweet Briar Lake (a ND designated Scenic Area), off I-94 exit 134 near New Salem. Primitive drive-in sites scattered around the lake's 10.5 miles of shoreline, large and well spaced, with picnic tables and fire rings; water pump at the first ramp. Two boat ramps with docks, floating and earthen fishing piers, picnic shelters. --Claude
summary: County page + parks FAQ: primitive camping $15/night (stored free $0 was wrong), FCFS, 10-night limit, no electric or site water, 6 vault toilets, potable water. Lakefront kept on imagery of the pin's loop point (no numbered sites). Phone missing: 701-667-3363.
flags: FEES CHANGE: stored 0/0 (free, from sweep prose) -> 15/15. The county parks FAQ: 'Primitive camping sites are $15/night'; Sweet Briar is not among the parks without camping, and offers 'Primitive Camping' only.

WATERFRONT (lakefront, check): kept on imagery, with a gap. The sites are unnumbered primitive spots scattered around the shore and no county map shows them. At the stored pin, a gravel loop road circles a small point (centre ~46.87355,-101.27455) with picnic tables on open grass 12-30 m from the water and only a thin rim of rushes at the shoreline; a rig parked on the loop's north edge sits ~20-25 m from the lake. A second loop on the north shore (~46.8760,-101.2722) carries shelters (picnic area). The south boat-ramp lot (~46.8680,-101.2752) is day use.
